Other armies fill the world map. About a fifth are faction armies of two hundred to a thousand troops, which stay inside their own country's borders. The rest are independent bands of five to thirty, which roam anywhere and spawn near you.

Touching one starts a field battle in a real time tactical view: your units in yellow, theirs in red, formed up by role, close quarters in front, support behind, ranged at the back, fighting on their own stats. Wounded troops drop to one hit point and stop; killed troops are gone for good.

societyMultiplayer.title: Multiplayer
societyMultiplayer.description:
Two ways to play with other people.

Online, through a central server or through Steam. A server session supports many players, of whom the nearest eight are drawn on one map. A Steam lobby caps at eight and sets rich presence, so friends see Join Game in their list.

Local split screen, two players on one machine with a gamepad each. The viewports are independent and merge into one when the players are close, and player two interacts with events directly.

Split screen also runs a hot seat for minigames without a split screen session on the overworld. Real time arcade carts let either player steer; chess, pool and bowling alternate turns.

During a map battle the viewports merge and player two drives the second party member.

societyHistory.title: The Century Behind You
societyHistory.description:
Before you take a step, the world has lived through a century: a generated alternate history of Europe from 1900 to 2001.

It produces coups, elections, purges and assassinations; wars, sieges, mutinies and conquests; fifty kinds of paranormal anomaly, occult rites and the Squishing itself; scientific expeditions, natural disasters and organised crime; economic shifts and technological breakthroughs. The weighting favours the paranormal and the occult.

That history sets which hyperpowers exist and how strong they are, which five sit on the Security Council, what epidemics the last century saw, and what the people you meet lived through.

The full timeline is readable in the Historical Archive.

econMoney.title: Money
econMoney.description:
Money is euros, written with two decimal places.

There is no other currency except at the arcade, where euros buy tokens and tokens sell back at a fixed rate.

The Assets screen adds cash, bank balance, property, shares and livestock, subtracts debts, and calls the result net worth.

econShops.title: Shops
econShops.description:
Shops come in several kinds.

- counter shop: a grid of goods with categories, sorted by price, with a detail card
- delivery order: arrives in one to seven days depending on price, up to six at once
- random daily shop: stock seeded from its coordinates and the world seed, rerolled every in game day
- vending machine: the same, in a 4x4 grid of coded products, three purchases per slot per day, with at least one odd item each
- teaching shop: sells skills instead of goods, at a discount

Tax is charged on everything except skills, at a rate that moves with the economy and never drops below thirty percent. A shop cleaned out restocks at midnight.

econStealing.title: Stealing
econStealing.description:
Anything on a shop's shelves can be stolen. The steal window scans the map for shop events and lists what they hold, with a success percentage per item computed from your agility, the item's value and its weight: light and cheap is easy, heavy and precious is not.

Ordinary shops are scanned across the whole map, a random daily merchant only within five tiles.

Getting caught files a crime and lowers the settlement's security. During a crime wave, stealing is measurably harder.

econBank.title: Banking and Loans
econBank.description:
The bank takes deposits, pays interest on the balance, and lends at interest against a due date. Both run on the world clock, so they accrue while you walk, sleep, travel or sit in cryogenic sleep.

Missing the due date is penalised. The Assets screen shows the balance, the outstanding loan and the date.

econStocks.title: The Stock Market
econStocks.description:
The market trades two commodities, oil and soul crystals, from a single page terminal. Prices are a random walk tilted by what happens in the world: settlement booms and busts, news events, the state of the powers.

The Assets screen draws the live graph over your portfolio. The oil price is also what the fuel pump charges and what a letter to another dimension costs.

econProperty.title: Real Estate
econProperty.description:
Thirty properties across the towns, rated one to five stars. A one star place costs under a thousand euros; four and five star places are estates.

Buy one outright and you can offer it for rent to NPCs, collected at midnight and on the first of the month. Rent it as a tenant and it is a recurring monthly cost, with no subletting; missed payments evict you.

Prices move with news events tied to specific towns.

Renting an inn room is separate: a room is booked for 24 game hours and cannot be double booked.

econShopOwning.title: Owning a Shop
econShopOwning.description:
A shop you own holds stock, a warehouse and a production line. Items with recipes can be produced from materials on the premises, deliveries are made at delivery points on the maps, and NPC staff can be hired to do the work.

Four pages: overview, shelf stock, warehouse, and the catalogue of what can be produced.

econWork.title: Work
econWork.description:
More than thirty jobs across several categories, and any party member can be sent to work.

Each job states its stat requirements first, and a member short of them is flagged but never blocked.

A shift takes game time, the screen darkens, and the outcome is generated from the worker's stats and luck. Pay is money; a disaster can cost money, deal damage, or leave a status effect.

The Job Offers menu lists what is available now and where.

econQuests.title: Quests
econQuests.description:
Quests are generated, and a board's offers are derived from where it stands.

Every quest is a list of steps: a simple quest has one, a chain two or three. The steps are detection primitives wired into the rest of the game:

- reach a set of world coordinates, or a named destination
- open an auto placed chest, or dig a site, which needs a shovel
- land on a planet and open its sample cache
- kill a specific high level enemy, force spawned at a tile, which stays there until killed even if the quest fails
- scan statues or signposts, or dismantle a number of trees, rocks or piles of rubble
- open the quest board of another town, or interview a citizen through Empathize
- hand over items, or wait for goods to arrive
- win arena fights, defeat a number of enemies, or hold a number of oil shares

Terms are shown before you accept: reward, upfront cost, advance paid, deadline, failure penalty, breach bounty and reputation change. Scams lie about them.

Rewards and difficulty scale on the party's median level. The board's second tab lists signed contracts with progress and countdowns, and lets you collect or abandon.

The quest log is a board of sticky notes in three columns, draggable between them.

econNotices.title: Reading a Notice
econNotices.description:
A quest notice is written in the voice of whoever pinned it up. Dozens of faction registers and a couple of dozen personality registers exist: a corporate contract, a goblin scrawl, a redacted military bill, a nervous private plea.

What is left out, what is over explained and what is plainly a lie are readable before you accept. The terms panel gives the numbers.

econVending.title: Arcade Tokens
econVending.description:
Arcade machines take tokens. Tokens are bought with euros at the converter machine or at the Token Exchange on the Hypernet, and unused tokens can be cashed back in.

Both quote the same rate.

craftThinker.title: The Workbench
craftThinker.description:
The Thinker is the general workbench: assembling and dismantling. The recipe is written on the item itself.

A recipe stays hidden until it has been made once, though common ones are on the board from the start.

Base materials come from dismantling the world: felling trees, mining rocks, breaking furniture, salvaging gear.

craftForge.title: The Forge
craftForge.description:
Every weapon and armour in the game is on the forge board from your first visit. Training changes which of them you can make.

Four tabs: what you can smith now, what you lack materials for, what is above your training, and what this party has already forged.

About thirty one trades are in play, one per item: a robe is Tailoring, a wig is Wig Making, a rifle is Gunsmithing, a circuit woven coat is Electronics.

Each finished piece is registered with its own identity, so two never stack. Three things set its sheet: how far past the required tier the smith's trade is trained, how rich the bill was, and the heat on the day. Every parameter then drifts on its own and the price follows.

Finishes are offered as a strip of swatches, and the seed the 3D model is turned under is rolled once and kept on the piece.

Smelt melts a carried piece back into materials: half the bill, more from a well made piece.

The party switcher decides which tab an entry falls into and who earns the specialization points.

craftAlchemy.title: Alchemistry
craftAlchemy.description:
Every alchemical recipe is readable from the start and nothing is gated behind a class.

A recipe is copied onto a bench, and the bench is what you edit and run, so one recipe can be set up two ways at once.

Success is a skill check. Meeting every requirement is 0% failure, each tier short raises the chance, and tiers above what the recipe asks pay out as extra product, up to a cap.

Step durations are game minutes, so a batch cooks while you walk, work, travel or sleep.

A bench set to repeat rebuys its reagents and starts again, and stands down with a warning when the pack cannot pay for a run.

craftCooking.title: Cooking
craftCooking.description:
Cooking combines two recovery items into one. The first item's recovery is doubled and the second's is added, so order matters.

Cooking two of the same thing adds a random adjective instead, carrying a bonus or a penalty. The name is built from the first word of the first ingredient and the last word of the second.

Food carries calories, fat and protein, and a cooked meal is worth what went into it.

craftBrewing.title: Brewing
craftBrewing.description:
Barrels ferment on the world clock. Load a barrel, leave it, and brewing and distilling proceed while you play.

It is the slowest crafting and needs no attention.

craftFurniture.title: Building and Furniture
craftFurniture.description:
The Build menu places furniture on tiles, snapped to the grid. Pieces can be crafted from materials, bought, and dismantled to recover them. Multi tile pieces are supported and some can be flipped.

Wall furniture goes on walls only, the upper tiles of ordinary furniture may overlap a wall but the lower tiles may not, and some terrain refuses furniture.

The Build menu is also where animals are bought.

craftPlants.title: Farming
craftPlants.description:
Any tilled soil can be farmed. Plants have a lifecycle driven by the clock, the season and the weather.

They grow only in their own seasons, and out of season they are dormant. Rain speeds growth by 30%, storms by 10%, snow halves it, and a greenhouse runs at full speed all year. A plant at 100% is harvested on the spot; the management menu only opens on a plot still growing.

Tilled soil on procedural maps is farmable too. The first visit to a world square rolls which patches are already sown and with what, so a whole field grows the same crop.

craftAnimals.title: Animals
craftAnimals.description:
Animals are bought in the Build menu and placed on a tile, then managed from the Assets screen as livestock to collect from, sell, or turn into a pet.

They grow from baby to adult over a set number of days, and adults produce at intervals: an egg, a pail of milk, a fleece.

Every animal carries a company value paid into the party's social need when you interact with it, once per game day. Dogs, donkeys and roosters produce nothing and are kept for this.

craftApiary.title: Beekeeping
craftApiary.description:
A hive is a colony simulation. Queen, workers, nurses, guards, foragers and drones each have a lifecycle from egg through larva and pupa to adult and death. The comb is drawn as hexagons, and the colony produces honey, pollen, royal jelly and wax.

Seasons and weather act on it, disease and pests threaten it, and its mood and efficiency follow how it is kept.

craftArtifacts.title: Procedural Artifacts
craftArtifacts.description:
Artifacts are generated items, weapons and armour with rolled properties. They appear in loot, in vaults, at the end of adventures, and from certain rites.

One rite turns a party member into a weapon.

craftLoot.title: How Loot Is Rolled
craftLoot.description:
Random loot is scored from 0 to 100: the party's median level plus a difficulty modifier carried by the place itself. The score picks the rarity band, from almost everything common at 0 to 20, through a balanced spread at 50, to almost everything legendary at 100.

Rarity is read off price, and the same ladder colours item names in the backpack, the shop, the reward popup and the container list.

A patron's vault pushes the tables toward the expensive end.

craftContainers.title: Containers
craftContainers.description:
Containers hold items without limit, and each is unique to its map and event. Contents are generated from the categories the container declares, weighted by rarity.

The extradimensional container can be opened from anywhere and travels with the party, as do the holds of the camper and the car.

galaxyOverview.title: The Star Map
galaxyOverview.description:
The star map is a real time 3D view of the universe at several scales: the system you are in, the galaxy, the local group, the supercluster, the cosmic web and the observable universe. At system scale one unit is one astronomical unit, and bodies are drawn larger than life to stay visible.

Drag to orbit, wheel to zoom. Clicking a body selects it and offers what you can do: travel there, or land.

Planets have day and night terminators tracking their own star, independently turning cloud layers, atmospheres and rings. Star surfaces boil.

galaxyTravel.title: Travelling Between Stars
galaxyTravel.description:
Select a system and travel to it. The journey takes time and burns fuel, and fuel sets your range.

Only an ordinary fusing star can power a refuel. Main sequence stars of every class work; remnants, brown dwarfs and black holes do not. Refuel starts the pumps if you are parked at one, plots a short hop if there is one elsewhere in the system, and otherwise plots a course to the nearest system that has one.

On any map inside the ship the windows show where you actually are, and they streak and scroll while under way.

galaxyShip.title: Your Starship
galaxyShip.description:
The ship is generated. Hull, layout, plating, panel lines, livery, decals, lit windows and wear are all procedural, and the default appearance comes from your world's seed.

From the vehicle menu you can reroll the whole thing or step through individual traits and keep the rest.

Under way the crew tends one need at a time: a meal, a wash, a conversation, a game, a shift of sleep. Eating consumes food from the hold.

galaxyLanding.title: Landing
galaxyLanding.description:
In orbit you can land. Where landing sites exist you pick from a list; otherwise you touch down on the surface.

An alien surface is an explorable map, generated like Earth's but from a different palette, with dozens of alien biomes chosen by the type of world.

- encounters are not scaled to your party or your distance from home. The planet's own level decides, readable from its biosignature before you commit
- there is nothing to forage. Food comes from butchering local wildlife
- a body stripped of its resources stays stripped

Identified species go into the bestiary's alien page.

galaxyAnomalies.title: Anomalies
galaxyAnomalies.description:
Every star system with planets carries at least one anomalous world, marked with a question mark.

Holding orbit over it offers to investigate, once only. What follows is a branching encounter written for that kind of world, paying out in a relic, in salvage, in a fight with something native, or in nothing.

It runs the same engine as the adventures on Earth's map.

galaxyBodies.title: What Is Out There
galaxyBodies.description:
Stars come in the real classes and in a couple of dozen exotic kinds, each with its own model: remnants, brown dwarfs, feeding X-ray binaries. Systems can be binary or hold several stars, each travelled to individually.

Black holes come in three weights, the largest drawn as lensed billboards with an accretion stream coiling across the whole separation. Rogue planets drift between the stars with no sun.

About twenty real nebulae sit at their real galactic coordinates, hand shaped: the Horsehead, the Orion Nebula, the dark nebulae. Dyson spheres exist.

Above the galaxy the map continues: local group, superclusters, cosmic web filaments and the shells of the observable universe.

Our own solar system is hand authored, with its twelve real bodies, its belts and a shell of orbital debris.

galaxyPatrons.title: Patron Worlds
galaxyPatrons.description:
Some worlds in other galaxies are named after the people who paid for the game. They are habitable and life bearing, they orbit exotic objects, they sit in nine planet systems where no two planets share a type, and they are listed in the star map catalogue under Patrons.

Each of those people also owns a hatch on exactly one world map square. It cannot be dismantled and nothing grows over it. Going down opens their vault: a great hall with strongrooms and a deep back chamber, filled with money and weapons, with the loot tables weighted to the expensive end.

Hatch locations are encrypted in the game data.

galaxySky.title: The Night Sky
galaxySky.description:
A night sky chart, separate from the star map: a draggable, zoomable planisphere with stars sized by magnitude, constellations traced in gold, a right ascension and declination grid, and a Milky Way band.

Tab switches between constellation sets, European and Chinese, which trace different figures over the same stars.

hypernetOS.title: The Hypernet Desktop
hypernetOS.description:
The Hypernet is a simulated operating system of the period: desktop, taskbar, start menu, draggable and resizable windows, and a set of applications.

It has a virtual file system and registry, both saved inside your savegame, so written files and changed settings persist.

- WASD or arrows move the focus ring, Tab cycles
- Enter or Space activates
- Escape leaves a text field, then closes the window, then exits
- on a controller: d-pad navigates, A activates, B closes, the left stick is a free cursor

hypernetBrowser.title: App: Hypernet Explorer
hypernetBrowser.description:
The browser. Tabs with their own history, back, forward, stop, refresh and home, an address bar with autocomplete, a links bar, an explorer bar with search, favorites and history, find on page, view source, saving a page, downloads, print preview, zoom, encoding, a pop up blocker, mail and news, and a 404 gateway page that suggests alternatives.

Every page in the archive is a full document. Preferences, favorites, history and downloads live in the registry and are kept in your savegame.

hypernetMyComputer.title: App: My Computer
hypernetMyComputer.description:
The file explorer. It browses the virtual file system: drives, folders, My Documents, and everything you or an application has written.

Files open in whichever application owns them: a text file in Notepad, a saved web page in the browser.

hypernetNotepad.title: App: Notepad
hypernetNotepad.description: A plain text editor writing into the virtual file system. Notes typed here are saved in your savegame, can be reopened, and can be read by any application that reads files.

hypernetControlPanel.title: App: Control Panel
hypernetControlPanel.description:
Machine settings. Your party's statistics are presented as hardware specifications. Wallpapers, display settings and the rest of the configuration live here.

Changes are stored in the registry.

hypernetTVGuide.title: App: TV Guide
hypernetTVGuide.description:
The television listings, read from the broadcast database. Browse every channel, its cast and its programmes.

Selecting a programme plays its broadcast inline, a line every couple of seconds, without leaving the desktop.

The schedule regenerates every in game week and is fixed for that week.

hypernetObjectIndex.title: App: The Object Index
hypernetObjectIndex.description:
The archive's catalogue of every object known to exist: about eleven hundred dossiers, one per item, with all declared metadata.

The left page is the catalogue, grouped by category, with a search box. The right page is the dossier: identification, lore paragraph, commerce, physical properties, provisioning values, composition and raw declaration tags.

The lore paragraph is combinatorial and resolved from the world seed. Randomize rerolls it for this window only.

hypernetNeuroPolice.title: App: N€police
hypernetNeuroPolice.description:
The continental police portal, for settling your criminal record without waiting to be caught.

- case file: every charge with its fine, settleable one at a time or all at once
- self-report: confess something not yet registered, at half the usual fine
- custody: turn yourself in, or request a hearing before Eris

The custody options close the computer, because the cells and the courtroom are places on the map.

hypernetEurodemics.title: App: Eurodemics
hypernetEurodemics.description:
The public terminal of the continental epidemic observatory, reading the live outbreak grimorie.

- situation: outbreaks running, people ill, people dead, towns affected, and a readout of where you are standing
- outbreaks: every outbreak burning, each with its daily curve, redrawn at midnight, over the town by town table
- archive: outbreaks this world has closed, plus the epidemics and mass hysterias of the last century

hypernetArtifactAnalyzer.title: App: Artifact Analyzer
hypernetArtifactAnalyzer.description: Analyses procedural artifacts and reports what they actually do.

hypernetTokenExchange.title: App: Token Exchange
hypernetTokenExchange.description: Converts euros into arcade tokens and back, at the same rate as the physical converter machine.

hypernetPhone.title: The Hexphone
hypernetPhone.description:
The party carries a mobile phone: credit, contacts, call history, an inbox and a couple of built in games.

Calling a contact triggers what that person does when called. Incoming calls arrive with an answer or decline prompt.

Keypad digits dial and act as shortcuts, Enter selects, calls and opens, Escape ends and goes back.

Payphones share the same contacts and credit grimorie, but only place outgoing calls: no inbox, no games, no incoming calls.

hypernetTV.title: Television
hypernetTV.description:
A television can be watched wherever you find one. Tuning to a channel puts you in that channel's studio, where the cast performs the broadcast: named cast turn to face you, take their own sprite and read their lines. A programme with no cast is narrated.

Dialogue is generated from templates over lore banks and splices in the live state of your world, so the history channel and the news desk read back the simulated century and the current news.

The weekly schedule regenerates every in game week. The script is rerolled on every tune in, ten to sixteen exchanges per slot.

Commercial breaks sell either a product, quoted at its real price, or a political position paid for by one of the powers.

Finishing a transmission raises the whole party's Fun; anyone with the Technophobe trait loses the same amount instead.

The channel guide is drawn as a forty by twenty five teletext page.

hypernetRadio.title: The Radio
hypernetRadio.description:
Radios tune across AM, FM and EM bands. The stations are built from the music files the game ships with, so every track is somewhere on the dial.

Left and right change frequency, up and down change band, page up and page down scan, Enter marks a favourite. Between stations there is static.

The last station tuned is remembered.

hypernetMusic.title: Music and Sound
hypernetMusic.description:
Battle music is chosen in Options. Random draws a different track at the start of every fight, and None fights in silence.

Map music is seeded: one track per combination of biome, nation and time of day. Some music is generated live by a procedural system.

Whatever plays announces itself, as a notification or as a drawn cassette, with track and artist.

Footsteps change with the surface underfoot.

gamesOverview.title: Diversions
gamesOverview.description:
The 3D games are simulations rendered through a retro shader, and most are played where you stand: the pool table, the basketball court, the bowling alley and the chess board are dropped into the scenery of the map you are on.

Playing anything feeds the whole party's Fun. Control hints are not printed; the keys are the ones you already use.

Two players can share almost all of them. Real time games let either player steer and turn based games become hot seat.

gamesArcade.title: The Arcade Cabinet
gamesArcade.description:
Arcade cabinets take tokens, bought with euros at the converter or on the Hypernet. A cabinet keeps high scores with letter entry and runs a demo when idle.

Each cart is a complete game, drawn in colour ASCII:

- Snake, against a red computer snake competing for the same apples
- Manpac, a pellet maze with three hunters and power pills that make them edible
- Frogger, across roads and rivers to five home slots
- Space Invaders, with destructible barriers
- Asteroids, with splitting rocks and a wrapping screen
- Breakout, with falling capsules
- Centipede, splitting when shot in the middle, with a spider that eats the mushrooms
- Bubble Pop, colours that stick and clusters that fall
- Boot sequence, a cabinet booting up and then a space to walk around in

gamesBowling.title: Bowling
gamesBowling.description:
A 3D alley with rigid body pin physics, simulated in metres at bowling dimensions: 18.29 metres to the head pin, a 1.07 metre lane, gutters, a 6.35 kilogram ball and 1.53 kilogram pins.

The camera rides the ball down the lane and cuts to the pin deck for the strike, and a rake sweeps deadwood between rolls.

Aim, power and spin use the oscillating slider shared with pool and basketball.

gamesPool.title: Pool
gamesPool.description:
A nine foot table simulated in metres. Balls roll under cloth friction, throw each other off on impact, rattle in the jaws of a pocket and drop.

Aim, power and spin are set with the oscillating slider. The table is dropped into whatever scenery you are standing in.

gamesBasketball.title: Basketball
gamesBasketball.description:
A free throw shootout against a computer opponent on a half court measured in metres: a 4.57 metre line, a rim 3.05 metres up, and a backboard.

The ball arcs under gravity, clatters off the rim, banks off the backboard and drops through the net, or misses.

gamesChess.title: Chess
gamesChess.description:
Full rules chess on a low poly 3D board. Every piece is a creature from the 3D battler system, dealt from the world seed, so one world always fields the same two armies: a bright one for White and a dark one for Black.

Two modes: normal chess and Chaos.

gamesFishing.title: Fishing
gamesFishing.description:
First person fishing. Fish, junk and hostile encounters are built by the same procedural battler system the battles use, so a Megalodon hooked in the lake is the Megalodon you then fight.

Aim by looking around. A ring on the water shows where the cast lands, then it is a contest between the line and whatever took it.

gamesSurfing.title: Surfing
gamesSurfing.description:
First person surfing. Every wave is a travelling swell with a tilted crest, so it peels: the breaking point races along the beach at about ten metres a second and the whitewater eats the wave behind it.

You stand on the board, which pitches, rolls and slaps across the chop. The game is reading the peel and staying ahead of it.

gamesShooting.title: The Shooting Range
gamesShooting.description:
A first person target range. The weapon in frame is the same 3D model the battle overlay raises, built, posed, aimed and fired by the weapon system, so every gun and bow handles as it does in a fight.

Nothing is equipped on your character: the range lends you the weapon and takes it back at the door, so it is also where a weapon can be tried before it is bought.

The rack holds only bows, projectile weapons and firearms.

gamesHorseRace.title: The Horse Race
gamesHorseRace.description:
A turf course in 3D: mown grass, running rails, a starting gate, distance poles, a winning post and a grandstand.

The runners are procedural creatures built from their own names: the name is hashed and handed to the battler system, which keys a coat, a colour and a build to it, so a named horse is the same horse in every world.

Odds are computed by simulating the race many times over the same step function the race then runs.

gamesTournament.title: The Monster Tournament
gamesTournament.description:
A single elimination monster tournament to bet on. Pick a fighter, place a bet in tokens, and only the fights involving your monster are shown.

The fights are run by the battle engine: the AI picks skills, pays costs, rolls to hit, evade and crit, applies damage formulas, inflicts states and ticks poison at end of turn. The result is then replayed in a 3D arena with animations.

Betting does not affect the outcome.

gamesGambling.title: Slots, Scratch Cards and Tarot
gamesGambling.description:
Slot machine: a cabinet whose reels are drums. Each symbol is a plate on a facet of a cylinder, so a spin turns the drum and a landing overruns its stop and springs back. The symbols come from the game's icon set.

Scratch cards: printed tickets rubbed panel by panel in any order, and the card can be turned in the light while you do it.

Tarot table: the deck riffles, the reader cuts it, the cards fly to their positions face down and turn one at a time.

gamesPiano.title: The Piano
gamesPiano.description:
A playable three octave keyboard, C3 to B5. It is played with the typing keyboard laid out as two manuals, whites on one row and blacks above, with a gamepad, or with the mouse. Keys light as they sound.

Playing it feeds the Fun need.

gamesLockpick.title: Lockpicking
gamesLockpick.description:
Picking a lock is a falling block puzzle: a key bit must fit into a partly packed keyway, and the lock's difficulty sets how hard the fit is.

Failure consumes a lockpick. A skeleton key skips the game and opens the lock outright.

Lockpicking opens locked doors and parked cars. Being caught at it is a crime.

gamesHyperTamer.title: HyperTamer
gamesHyperTamer.description:
A virtual pet on a monochrome LCD handset, drawn from the creature database and given a personality that changes how it behaves.

It runs on real time: it eats, sleeps, plays and can die of neglect, and time passes while the game is closed. Training minigames raise its stats and it grows accordingly.

gamesCards.title: The Card Game
gamesCards.description:
A collectible card game with a collection, a deck builder and duels.

A card is a monster, a weapon or a piece of armour from the game's database, printed with five stats, STR, WIS, DEX, PSI and CON, each from 0 to 13. Those numbers are percentiles against that card's own roster, not raw parameters. Equipment is bolted onto a monster already on the board and its values are added, clamped to 13.

A deck is 9 to 20 cards and may only hold copies you own. A player who never opens the deck builder is dealt the best legal deck their collection allows.

A duel is three by three. On your turn you either draw three cards or place one: a monster onto a free tile, or gear onto one of your own monsters, one weapon and one armour each.

When the last tile is taken, every monster looks at its four orthogonal neighbours, picks the weakest enemy among them and fights it. Every pairing is scored against one frozen snapshot of the board and all deaths land together. Most stats won takes the fight, an equal count destroys both. Whoever has more monsters standing wins, ties broken on the summed stats of the survivors.

Booster packs hold six cards from one pool, weighted so the last is never common.

Cards are also won by capturing a creature in battle. Capture picks the weakest creature still standing, helped by the caster's PSI against its own, and is impossible against anything more than ten levels above your median. Success adds the card and kills the creature, so the spoils still drop.

gamesRaman.title: The Raman Scanner
gamesRaman.description: A spectroscopy scanner that analyses the object you are facing: statues, paintings, masks, bookcases and library objects. It identifies the material, draws its Raman spectrum, and pays knowledge points.

gamesPeriodic.title: The Periodic Table
gamesPeriodic.description: A viewer for the periodic table, laid out as a book: the full grid on the left page, lanthanides, actinides and a set of esoteric elements that appear in no real table, with the selected element's description on the right.

arcaneSurge.title: State: Arcane Surge
arcaneSurge.description: Increases magic power but consumes MP each turn. It raises INT by 50%, raises WIS by 50% and drains 10% of max MP every turn. It lasts 3-5 actions.

berserk.title: State: Berserk
berserk.description: Increases attack power but decreases defense and makes target attack randomly. It raises STR by 50% and lowers CON by 30%. The afflicted attacks anyone at random, ally or enemy. It lasts 2-4 actions.

bleeding.title: State: Bleeding
bleeding.description: It drains 10% of max HP every turn. It does not wear off on its own. And it follows you out of the fight.

blind.title: State: Blind
blind.description: It lowers accuracy by 50%. It lasts 3-5 actions.

burned.title: State: Burned
burned.description: It drains 10% of max HP every turn. It does not wear off on its own. And it follows you out of the fight.

charm.title: State: Charm
charm.description: It carries no stat change of its own. The afflicted turns on their own side. It lasts 2-4 actions. A solid hit can break it early.

cold.title: State: Cold
cold.description: It lowers ice damage taken 50%, raises STR by 10% and raises fire damage taken 200%. It lasts 5 turns.

confusion.title: State: Confusion
confusion.description: It carries no stat change of its own. The afflicted attacks anyone at random, ally or enemy. It lasts 2-4 actions. A solid hit can break it early.

shadow.title: State: Shadow Veil
shadow.description: Makes target harder to hit but also reduces their accuracy. It lowers accuracy by 40% and lowers how often it is targeted by 50%. It lasts 2-4 actions.

silence.title: State: Silence
silence.description: It seals a school of skills. It lasts 3-5 actions.

sleep.title: State: Sleep
sleep.description: It lowers evasion by 100%. The afflicted cannot act at all. It lasts 3-5 turns. A solid hit can break it early.

static.title: State: Static
static.description: It lowers thunder damage taken 50% and raises STR by 10%. It lasts 5 turns.

stun.title: State: Stun
stun.description: It lowers evasion by 100%. The afflicted cannot act at all. It lasts 1-2 turns.

unbalanced.title: State: Unbalanced
unbalanced.description: Target has a chance to fail their action at the end of each turn. It lowers accuracy by 30%. It lasts 1-3 actions. A solid hit can break it early.

vulnerability.title: State: Vulnerability
vulnerability.description: Decreases the target's physical defense. It lowers CON by 50%. It does not wear off on its own. And it follows you out of the fight.

wet.title: State: Wet
wet.description: It lowers fire damage taken 50% and raises thunder damage taken 100%. It lasts 5 turns.

immortal.title: State: Immortal
immortal.description: It wards off Dead. It lasts 1-2 turns.

poison.title: State: Poison
poison.description: It drains 5% of max HP every turn. It does not wear off on its own. Walking it off works too, and it follows you out of the fight.

rage.title: State: Rage
rage.description: It raises STR by 50%. The afflicted attacks an enemy at random and cannot be commanded. It lasts 2-4 actions. A solid hit can break it early.

freeze.title: State: Freeze
freeze.description: It lowers evasion by 100%, seals a school of skills and seals a school of skills. The afflicted cannot act at all. It lasts 3 turns.

paralysis.title: State: Paralysis
paralysis.description: It lowers evasion by 100%. The afflicted cannot act at all. It lasts 3 turns.

lockedOn.title: State: Locked on
lockedOn.description: Increases critical rate It raises critical rate by 300%. It lasts 2-4 actions.

hpRegeneration.title: State: HP Regeneration
hpRegeneration.description: It restores 10% of max HP every turn. It lasts 4 turns.

mpRegeneration.title: State: MP Regeneration
mpRegeneration.description: It restores 10% of max MP every turn. It lasts 4 turns.

apRegeneration.title: State: AP Regeneration
apRegeneration.description: It restores 10% of max AP every turn. It lasts 4 turns.

magicReflection.title: State: Magic Reflection
magicReflection.description: It raises magic reflection by 100%. It lasts 5 turns.

protect.title: State: Protect
protect.description: It changes how the battler behaves. It lasts 1 turn.

provoke.title: State: Provoke
provoke.description: It raises how often it is targeted by 800%. It lasts 5 turns.

hide.title: State: Hide
hide.description: It stops how often it is targeted entirely. It lasts 5 turns.

counterAttack.title: State: Counter Attack
counterAttack.description: It raises counter rate by 100%. It lasts 3 actions.

statusAilmentBlock.title: State: Status Ailment Block
statusAilmentBlock.description: It wards off 9 different conditions. It lasts 5 turns.

inspired.title: State: Inspired
inspired.description: Reduces MP cost. It lowers MP cost by 75%. It lasts 5 turns.

hot.title: State: Hot
hot.description: It raises water damage taken 100%, raises STR by 10% and lowers petro damage taken 50%. It lasts 5 turns.

divineShield.title: State: Divine Shield
divineShield.description: Cuts every incoming element by 30% and makes critical hits impossible. Lasts 3-5 turns.

deathMark.title: State: Death Mark
deathMark.description: Raises every kind of damage taken by 30% and pulls almost every attack onto the target. Lasts 2-3 actions.

perfectFocus.title: State: Perfect Focus
perfectFocus.description: Guarantees critical hits but reduces defense. It raises critical rate by 100% and lowers CON by 20%. It lasts 2-3 turns.

ethereal.title: State: Ethereal
ethereal.description: Physical damage passes through harmlessly, every magical element hits twice as hard. Lasts 3-5 turns.

lifeLink.title: State: Life Link
lifeLink.description: Damage taken is shared among all party members. It carries no stat change of its own. It lasts 3-5 turns.

nausea.title: State: Nausea
nausea.description: It lowers AGI by 25%. It does not wear off on its own. And it follows you out of the fight.

drunk.title: State: Drunk
drunk.description: It drains 40% of max AP every turn. It does not wear off on its own. A solid hit can break it early, walking it off works too, and it follows you out of the fight.

infected.title: State: Infected
infected.description: It drains 10% of max HP every turn. It does not wear off on its own. And it follows you out of the fight.

floating.title: State: Floating
floating.description: It raises thunder damage taken 100%, raises STR by 10%, makes petro damage harmless and lowers physical damage taken 50%. It lasts 5 turns.

invisible.title: State: Invisible
invisible.description: It raises evasion by 999%, raises magic evasion by 999%, raises critical evasion by 999% and lowers how often it is targeted by 70%. It lasts 3 turns. A solid hit can break it early.

oily.title: State: Oily
oily.description: It raises fire damage taken 899%. It lasts 5 turns.

dodge.title: State: Dodge
dodge.description: It raises evasion by 200% and raises magic evasion by 200%. It lasts 1 turn.

withdrawal.title: State: Withdrawal
withdrawal.description: It lowers STR by 15%, lowers INT by 15%, lowers DEX by 10%, lowers accuracy by 15% and lowers evasion by 5%. It does not wear off on its own. And it follows you out of the fight.

grappled.title: State: Grappled
grappled.description: Held in a lock. Agility and evasion collapse and physical blows land harder. It lowers DEX by 60%, lowers evasion by 60% and raises physical damage taken by 25%. It lasts 2-3 turns.

pinned.title: State: Pinned
pinned.description: Pinned to the ground and unable to act. One solid hit shakes it loose. It lowers evasion by 90%. The afflicted cannot act at all. It lasts 1-2 turns. A solid hit can break it early.

guardBroken.title: State: Guard Broken
guardBroken.description: Their defence is prised open: defence halved and guarding does nothing. It lowers CON by 50%, lowers WIS by 20% and stops guarding entirely. It lasts 2 turns.

winded.title: State: Winded
winded.description: The breath is gone: slower, and no stamina builds up while it lasts. It lowers DEX by 20%, lowers AP charge rate by 65% and drains 5% of max MP every turn. It lasts 3 turns.

comboReady.title: State: Combo Ready
comboReady.description: The opening has been read and the follow-up is loaded. Some techniques hit far harder with it. It raises accuracy by 20% and raises critical rate by 15%. It lasts 2 turns.

vitalExposed.title: State: Vital Exposed
vitalExposed.description: A vital point is uncovered. Every physical blow that follows does half again as much. It raises physical damage taken by 50% and lowers critical evasion by 30%. It lasts 2-3 turns.

rootedStance.title: State: Rooted Stance
rootedStance.description: Planted and immovable: much harder to hurt or knock over, and slower for it. It raises CON by 40%, lowers DEX by 30% and wards off 3 different conditions. It lasts 4 turns.

flowState.title: State: Flow State
flowState.description: Reading the blow before it is thrown: turns attacks aside and answers some of them. It raises counter rate by 25%, raises evasion by 20% and lowers physical damage taken by 15%. It lasts 3 turns.

chiBurn.title: State: Chi Burn
chiBurn.description: The price of spending everything at once. The body keeps paying for a while. It drains 4% of max HP every turn, lowers INT by 15% and lowers AP charge rate by 50%. It lasts 3 turns.

concussed.title: State: Concussed
concussed.description: A blow to the head. Nothing aims true and nothing thinks straight. It lowers INT by 30%, lowers WIS by 30% and lowers accuracy by 20%. It lasts 2-3 turns.
